gaps.sentence: My boss won't ___ me take Friday off.
gaps.explanation: let + object + bare infinitive: won't let me take. (allow/permit take to: allow me to take.)

gaps.sentence: She was the first woman ___ the peak in winter.
gaps.explanation: the first/second/last + to-infinitive: the first woman to climb.

gaps.sentence: It took me ages ___ used to the new keyboard.
gaps.explanation: it takes time + to-infinitive: took me ages to get used to the keyboard.

gaps.sentence: We'd better not ___ the neighbours again.
gaps.explanation: had better + bare infinitive (not comes after better): better not disturb.

gaps.sentence: Do you want me ___ you at the station?
gaps.explanation: want + object + to-infinitive: want me to meet.

gaps.sentence: I can't wait ___ you the photos.
gaps.explanation: can't wait + to-infinitive: can't wait to show.

gaps.sentence: He apologised for ___ so rude to the waiter.
gaps.explanation: 'Apologise for being' — 'for' is a preposition, so the gerund follows.

gaps.sentence: He spent hours ___ to fix the printer.
